case_title: MOHD. JALEES ANSARI AND OTHERS v. CENTRAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
statutory_provisions: Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 ss. 3, 4, 5 and 6; IPC s. 302, 307, 324, 326 and 436; Explosive Substance Act, 1908 ss. 3 and 4; Explosives Act, 1884 s.9B; Railways Act, 1989 ss. 150 and 151; Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984 s.4
confession: Confessional statements of A-1, A-2, A-3, A-4, A-7, A-14, A-15 and A-16 are admissible; confessions of A-5, A-8, A-9, A-10, A-11 and A-13 cannot be relied upon as substantive pieces of evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Bomb blasts in trains, use of explosives, conspiracy
offence_finally_established: Bomb blasts under TADA Act and IPC
neutral_facts: The accused were involved in a conspiracy to cause bomb blasts in different trains. Confessional statements of some accused were recorded, which were corroborated by other evidence. The prosecution relied on these confessions and circumstantial evidence to establish the case against the accused. The confessions of some accused were found to be unreliable or not admissible. The trial court convicted several accused, but the Supreme Court upheld their convictions after reviewing the evidence and the admissibility of confessions. The court also set aside the convictions of some accused due to lack of evidence. The bomb blasts caused injuries and deaths, and the accused were involved in planning and executing the attacks using explosives.
